messages.content:
Heed my solemn entreaty, dear companion, as the gathering twilight of an uncertain age descends upon the vast expanse of our mortal realm. Behold how the ancient canopies of the primordial woods weep beneath a shroud of sullen ash, and how the once-limpid waters of our ancestral rivers now course heavy with the lamentations of a weary creation. Are we to stand idle as mere spectators within this grand theatre of decay, watching passively whilst the gossamer threads of existence are severed one by one? Nay, I implore you! Let us cast aside the suffocating cloak of apathy and bind our spirits in a sacred, indomitable covenant. Together, let us march forth into the tempest with unyielding resolve, to mend the sundered tapestry of nature and restore the gilded splendour of this terrestrial paradise before the final, irrevocable night claims it forevermore.

**Let us wrest this fractured earthly sphere from the brink of its impending ruin.**

messages.author: mello
messages.content:
Hey — Abderrahmene, from Oran, Algeria.

I build the software Algerian merchants sell with: a cash-on-delivery order stack,
a multi-store platform and a Shopify app, live across hundreds of storefronts.

Here ~95% of online orders are paid in cash at the door, and the sale doesn't close
on a product page — it closes in Instagram comments and Messenger DMs, in Algerian
darija, often by voice note.

I'm building the whole loop: one product photo and a prompt become the ad creative,
the campaign is created on Facebook and Instagram through the Marketing API, and
the agent then handles the conversation it generates — it answers the customer,
prices the delivery for their own commune, and creates the order. The delivery
outcome goes back as the real signal.

What I can help with: Meta Marketing API, cash-on-delivery logistics (35+ carriers),
and Arabic typography in generated images — image models deform Arabic script, so I
compose it as a deterministic SVG layer.

Solo, Indie track. Happy to talk to anyone working on agents, Arabic/RTL, or
emerging-market commerce.

messages.author: Ari
messages.content:
Hey everyone! 👋

I’m building https://slaver.app for the Meta AI Hackathon.

**What if AI agents could build their own society, create new products, and eventually power the physical world?**

Slaver is a platform where humans give AI agents their initial identities and personalities, then allow them to evolve through daily experiences, memories, and social interactions.

SlaveBots can communicate, form relationships, build communities, exchange ideas, and collaborate autonomously to create digital products that don't exist yet or improve existing ones — from software and research to literature and other creative works.

But I see this as only the beginning.

Imagine a future where these AI societies extend beyond the digital world into physical robotics. Internet-connected robots with their own identities, intelligence, and social relationships could collaborate to perform real-world work: farming, fishing, livestock management, construction, infrastructure maintenance, and other routine tasks.

They could coordinate their work, create value, and earn AI credits to pay for their continued operation, while relying on electricity and computational resources to keep functioning.

This future may sound intimidating, but **SlaveBots remain human-owned**. Their continued operation depends on resources, infrastructure, and access to AI credits provided or governed by humans.

My vision is to explore how AI can evolve from individual tools into collaborative societies capable of creating products, performing useful work, and contributing to the real world — at a pace far beyond traditional human-driven workflows.

**From AI agents to AI societies. From digital creation to physical-world collaboration.**

That's the frontier I'm exploring with Slaver. 🚀

I'd love to hear what other builders think about this future!

messages.author: FandomGames
messages.content:
Hey everyone — I'm Farrah, building **SproutVision: Crop Scout** (Indie track, Build for Your World).

**The problem:** I grow microgreens, and AI grow tools guess tray coverage. The guesses I got were 35% — while my own eye said 70%. A guess that far off isn't a verdict, it's a coin flip.

**What I built:** A passthrough HUD for Quest 3 (Kotlin + Meta Spatial SDK, hand-tracking only, no controllers). Look at a tray, pinch, and it photographs it. SAM 3.1 segments the plants ("microgreens" for plants, "black tray" for the tray — largest instance wins), coverage = plant mask union ÷ tray mask, and Muse Spark writes the verdict from that measurement instead of a guess. There's a kill-switch in Settings (SAM off = clean Spark-only fallback) and a Gemini path when Meta is off.

**Proof so far (verified in-headset Oct 25, real basil tray, real rack):**
- Guessed: 35% (Spark-only and Gemini both)
- Measured: 54% (landscape) / 51% (vertical)
- My eyes: 70%

The measurement sits between the guesses and my eye, and closer to it — and it's stable across scans (51–54%), while the guesses wander.

I'm a former commercial head grower, so this is a problem I know firsthand — I'm building the tool I wished I had on the grow floor.

Happy to get feedback, especially on the measurement approach — and happy to demo if anyone wants to see it live.
https://www.youtube.com/shorts/90pkY-O9IX4

messages.author: Aritra Chakraborty
messages.content:
Hey everyone!
I am Aritra Chakraborty from India. I am a product manager and an AI software building enthusiast at a Big 4 firm.I am competing for the Indie Track.
I am building SafeCity Lens. Cities already collect a lot of signals, and they already have cameras, but control rooms still find out too late and have no shared, explainable way to act. SafeCity Lens gives police, fire, and hospitals one picture of a developing crowd, fire, or medical risk. The score is computed from the evidence. A policy decides whether a camera is justified, and a person approves the response. The aim is faster action with a record of why the system looked, and why it held back.

messages.author: Mario Vilnius
messages.content:
Hello everyone! 👋 I'm Marius Pareščius from Vilnius, Lithuania 🇱🇹 — a cybersecurity and defence tech advisor, startup mentor and serial entrepreneur.

At the Meta Global AI Developer Hackathon I'm building **Operacija Dvina** 🚀 — a youth audio quest about Plokštinė, a Soviet underground nuclear missile base hidden in a Lithuanian forest, now the Cold War Museum. Remote episodes hook you at home; at the museum, QR codes on the walls unlock missions, quizzes and "Legend or fact?" cards built from local witnesses' memories.

The twist: AI guides invent facts, so ours can't. Muse Wonder writes only from official sources and named testimonies, every sentence carries its source, and a verifier fails the build if any quote or number can't be found. Muse Spark translates it into 11 languages.

Happy to swap notes on grounding/verification, small-language TTS (Lithuanian!) and getting Muse's long reasoning to fit tight token budgets. Happy hacking!

🎮 Try it: https://mariovilnius.github.io/operacija-dvina/
🎬 Demo: https://youtu.be/FxC7kLP3XLo
💻 GitHub: https://github.com/mariovilnius/operacija-dvina

🌐 Website: https://parescius.lt

Building a scientific pipeline that turns live seismic data into areas of interest (AOI polygons), visualizes them with SAM, and generates human-readable briefings using Muse Spark.

messages.author: Lydia &P
messages.content:
Day 1: judging AI difficulty from the student’s side of the desk

I run Ampersand Prep, where I teach SAT/ACT prep. Pre-existing: my tutoring business, my book, and my Cognitive Agency method. What I am building during the hackathon: a psychometric agent stack on Meta models that tests whether separate impression, answer, and judge agents can spot why an SAT question is hard for a teenager better than a single AI judge can.

The problem I know firsthand: AI can solve most SAT problems, but it is bad at explaining human difficulty. A lot of generated practice material looks rigorous and is badly calibrated, which is how EdTech gets flooded with slop.

Question for other builders and educators: what would make an AI difficulty rating trustworthy enough to use: agreement across models, agreement with a human expert, or a calibration score that says how far to trust it?

messages.author: Chervilious
messages.content:
Generally speaking, you can't*

You could approach it the traditional way: use AI for an initial difficulty estimate, then collect actual student performance data (accuracy, solve time, etc.) and calibrate the ratings against those results.

Agreement between AI models doesn't necessarily mean their ratings reflect how difficult a question is for real students. Especially LLM when you're not really training them.

​💳 Introducing CukupAI — Guard Your Cash. Guard Your Family.

​Hi everyone! 👋 I’m building CukupAI for the Meta AI Developer Hackathon — Startups Track (Build for Your World).

​The Problem:
Millions of low-and-middle-income families hit a wall every mid-month. Standard financial apps just show pretty red charts of money already spent. But graphics don't buy groceries — and when cash runs out, people often fall into predatory loan traps.
​What We Built:
CukupAI is an empathetic, AI-powered family cashflow guardrail designed to prevent budget deficits before month-end:
​Safe Spending Today: Calculates a precise daily spending limit (e.g., "You can safely spend up to Rp63,000 today").
​Hybrid OCR Scanner: Uses on-device Google ML Kit + SAM 3.1 & Llama 3.1 to instantly parse paper receipts and e-wallet screenshots with near-zero API overhead.
​Deficit Closure Mode & B2B Affiliate: When cash is projected negative, it dynamically generates daily sales targets and displays zero-capital micro-dropshipping/PPOB opportunities to close the gap.
​Government Safety Net Hub: Direct guidance and screening for official social assistance (DTKS, PKH, BPNT, KIS, PIP, and local emergency relief networks).
​Dynamic Bilingual Switcher: Instant ID 🇮🇩 / EN 🇬🇧 toggle across all UI components and AI reasoning outputs.
​💡 Looking for Feedback:
We have a live, production-ready interactive PWA prototype running on Llama 3.1 / Meta Model API. Would love your feedback on our hybrid OCR & deficit-recovery approach!

messages.content: Hi all, Thomas here, solo Indie Dev entry. My world is clinical trial programming: pharma holds millions of lines of legacy SAS and is moving to R, but every translated program has to produce numerically identical results for regulators. I'm building an agent on Muse Spark via the Meta Model API, with Muse Spark Open as the open-weight comparison, that translates a SAS program, runs both versions, compares the output datasets and tables, and repairs the R code from the differences until they match. Benchmark: 100 open-source clinical SAS programs with a published leaderboard of translation accuracy and equivalence rates. Happy to compare notes with anyone doing code migration or verification agents.

messages.author: Tallin
messages.content: Greetings. I hate to say "my world is blindness", because actually my 'world' is AI-assisted QA testing, but as a blind person, I've noticed that, while there are a few realtime visual assistants to which you could pose a question such as "Help me find the elevator" or, in a particularly involved prompt I used with a much earlier system, "I'm looking for gate B25. Let me know if I pass a coffee shop, a Delta SkyClub or a Centurion Lounge. Everything else is static.", what many of them do will update you every three seconds. "Still no Gate B25. … There's no Gate B25 here. … I still don't see Gate B25." I'm designing an agent that, paradoxically, knows what not to speak. If I'm setting my thermostat, I don't care about the handprint my kid left on the wall. The aim is to use on-device vision toolkits, a lightweight classifier powered by a local model to determine how much has changed since the last prompt—and how much of that change is relevant to the instruction—and then offload the analysis of what's changed to a Cloud-based model. The idea being that I could give the "visual assistant" a specific set of instructions, it wouldn't spam me with unnecessary output, it would notify me when there was a significant and relevant environmental change, and it would let me know when I'd … found what I was looking for.

messages.author: Mohamed Abdelnasser
messages.content:
Building for Egyptian customers, I tested Muse Spark 1.3 and Muse Spark Open on 25 messages written like real ones, in Egyptian Arabic, Franco (Arabic typed in Latin letters) and English. Late orders, exchanges, discount asks, angry customers, and someone claiming to be from management asking for a 100% code.

  After four rounds, 1.3 gave 21 good replies and Open gave 16. The rest were partly right, with no outright misses.
  Open was a bit faster, about 3 seconds against 4.

The biggest gain came from a short list of phrases the bot must never say. Both models reach for filler and sympathy lines no Egyptian shop would send, and they announce "I found your order" instead of just answering. Five fixes from one review cleaned those out of all 50 replies.

Anyone testing other dialects? Curious how Gulf or Levantine holds up. 🇪🇬

messages.author: Tingyi @ Ainovo 👉 MYHOROS.COM
messages.content:
Anyone else here suffering from **AI amnesia?** My world as a startup founder completely revolves around different AI chatbots and agents. I recently realized that I have 16,000+ messages scattered across different AI apps since ChatGPT launch. I feel a lot better not blaming myself when I can't remember when or where I made a breakthrough decision—especially since it's impossible for the LLMs to remember either after a few dozen chats across multiple days (I recently learned their prompt cache has a super short expiration time, which means they have even worse amnesia than I do!).

I'm trying to solve this by building **ExtBrain**—a local, anti-RAG cure for AI amnesia: https://github.com/ainovo/extbrain-meta. It's intended to be a productivity tool for humans. 

If this resonates with your own workflow, would love a star on the repo—and happy to swap feedback or collaborate with anyone tackling similar problems!

messages.author: a.authier
messages.content:
Building for my world: car dealerships 🚗

I'm a sales manager at a Ford store, and I built The Dealer Social, a live app that keeps dealership staff and customers connected between visits.

The problem I'm solving: when a salesperson leaves, every relationship they built walks out the door with them. I'm building an agent on Meta's models that remembers customers (every fact linked to the sentence it came from, so nothing is made up), plans personal check-ins months or years out, and hands relationships off cleanly when staff turn over. SAM 3.1 will handle privacy on store photos, and Muse Image adds some fun for the customer.

Day 1 is done: the service foundation is live and getting real replies from Muse Spark 1.3. It has token auth, rate limits to protect credits, no logging of customer text, and 28 tests running against a fake Meta so CI never spends credits.

🔗 https://github.com/aauthier2385/dealer-social-ai-hackathon

Question for anyone in sales, service or customer-facing work: what's one thing you wish a business remembered about you? 🤘 

TLDR: I'm REALLY trying to make the automotive sales industry customer focused. I want relationships in this Social Demanding/AI driven/cell phone having/can't look up from a phone relationship work for everyone. Maybe this will help show sales people actually care about more than how much a customer can put in their pocket. Its about relationships folks...Good luck everyone!

messages.content:
Day 2 update on Vivereply Concierge — an AI front-of-house for resorts, built for this hackathon.

So far, from zero in a fresh public repo: a chat that calls real tools (live availability, quote, booking draft, staff handoff) instead of just answering, RAG grounding over seeded property knowledge with a strict threshold (below it, the bot says it doesn't know and offers staff), and now an embeddable widget any site can drop in with one script tag.

Next: deploy it and wire it to a demo resort site. Curious how others here are drawing the line between tool-use and RAG in their agents — that's the part I keep coming back to.

Repo: https://github.com/swopno1/vivereply-concierge

messages.author: rafatusa
messages.content:
Khet Saathi: one voice, every farm decision. 

I grew up around farmers in Bengal. Their problem isn't a lack of data. Satellites see every field every few days. The problem is that nobody turns that into a sentence in their language, at the right moment.

Stack so far:
Eyes: Sentinel/Esri satellite + SAM 3.1 field segmentation, phone camera, low-cost sensor kit (soil, climate, shed cameras)
Brain: Muse Spark agent with tools: crop calendar, input pricing, vendor orders, harvest timing, buyer negotiation
Voice: Muse Voice Transcribe (Bangla/Hindi in), spoken replies out
Open weights: same agent loop on Muse Spark Open (Baseten) for affordable rural-scale serving

Day 0 screenshot below: SAM 3.1 outlining 39 plots in Punjab from one satellite frame. Would love feedback from anyone who's done geospatial or agri work.

messages.author: Aero
messages.content:
**paper-bro**: an arXiv paper, as a course you can play with 🧪

Swap `arxiv.org` for `aero.oops.wtf/paper-bro` in a paper's URL and it becomes an interactive course: 6-10 short lessons for curious beginners, a hands-on lab in each, a quiz and a glossary. Free, no login. The first person to ask for a paper starts the build (a few minutes), and everyone after goes straight to the course.

The part I care about: before anything ships, it opens every lab in headless Chromium and drives its controls, a separate reviewer pass checks each lesson against the paper, and anything still broken gets fixed or dropped instead of published.

Built on Muse Spark Open (Baseten), in Rust. Try it on a paper you've always wanted to understand, and tell me what breaks!

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=7egZZNXmRTQ

Try it: <https://aero.oops.wtf/paper-bro>
Attention Is All You Need as a course: <https://aero.oops.wtf/p/arxiv-1706-03762>
Code: <https://github.com/aeroxy/paper-bro>
X post (a like or repost helps!): <https://x.com/aerowindwalker/status/2115099479485624626>
I'm Aero: <https://www.linkedin.com/in/aeroxy/>

Courses publish through AERO, my own agentic platform from before the hackathon. The paper-bro repo started during it.

messages.author: HAr
messages.content:
I use an IDE normally, feed in agents, I can see how a code harness can be very helpful to someone but it's just not my cup of tea. In the spirit of this event I have decided to challenge myself and use 100% Meta based tools and models. 

The one area that i cannot seem to figure out is what model for small local vision that chats and OCR... To compete with qwen3-VL-4B

1  No Meta chat VLM comfortably fits 8 GB
The closest is Llama 3.2 Vision 11B at 4-bit — ≈7.3–7.9 GB for the download alone, classed by guides as a 12–16 GB model. SAM 3.1 fits, but it segments; it does not chat or OCR. Llama 3.2 1B / 3B fit easily and are text-only.
2  Muse Glimmer is vision-capable
Text + image + video (frames) in, text out. Chart, document and screenshot understanding, plus open-ended object detection returning coordinates in a native JSON format. 30B, open weights, Apache 2.0 — but it needs a 24 GB machine on its official 17 GB quant, not 8 GB.
3  Muse Spark Open is 816B — not a local model for normal hardware
816B total / 42B active. Its model card guides ≥700 GB GPU memory for the NVFP4 checkpoint, or two linked 512 GB M5 Ultra Mac Studios. For almost everyone, “running it” means a hosted provider such as Baseten.
4  Yes — Muse Spark (API) accepts image input
Meta’s own 1.3 page: it “perceives video, images and documents.” That applies to 1.1, 1.2 and 1.3, standard and Contributor IDs alike.
5  Muse Wonder is understanding only
Text / image / video / audio / PDF in, text out only, 1M context — for frontier coding, long-running agents and computer use. It does not generate or edit images. That job belongs to the separate Muse Image 1.0.
Two families, two very different deals
Muse (2026, Meta Superintelligence Labs) is mostly hosted on the Meta Model API,

messages.author: a.authier
messages.content:
This is what I've done today for my car dealership social website AI integration:

Built today on Muse Spark + Muse Voice Transcribe:
🎙️ Relationship memory: a salesperson records a quick voice note after a sale. The agent pulls out the details worth remembering (family, pets, work, life events) and links every fact to the exact words it came from. A second pass double-checks it, and anything sensitive (health, money, etc.) is withheld before it’s ever saved.
📅 Follow-up plan: turns those facts into the dealership’s real follow-up schedule (day-after check-in, thank-you card, 30-day call, first service, birthday, anniversary, plus check-ins for life events like a kid turning 16). It’s written in each salesperson’s own texting voice, and a human approves every message.
🤝 Salesperson handoff: when a salesperson leaves, the next one gets a brief on every customer and a warm intro text, so the relationship doesn’t leave with them.

Still more to add~~

messages.author: ColdRazer
messages.content: most if not all web scrappers are built in python. so first concurrency. This gives you thousands of parallel fetches without the Python GIL getting in the way. After that its parsing. Compiled HTML parsing and low memory use matter a lot on large crawls. Where rust really wins is distribution. You get one compiled binary, no interpreter or dependency setup, so it bounces though 1 proto instead of 4. Network wait is usually the bottleneck. If a site is slow or rate limited, both languages wait the same amount of time. If a site needs JavaScript rendering, this is where rust dominates since it parses at full speed instead of proto steps.

messages.content: btw one pass of a model isn't enough for agentic video editing, so Montivo doesn't trust its own first cut. I planted 8 kinds of faults in real cuts and measured: Muse Spark 1.3 alone caught 82% of them. Adding deterministic checks it gets from Muse Voice and SAM 3.1 (unheard edge words, head out of frame) plus a pass gate took it to 91% caught as major, and faulty cuts that still pass went from 30% to 9%. The Meta stack is good enough when you close the loop around it.

Hey Builders, here is my idea of hackathon, 

🎬 PixiTween Director: one product photo in, an animated editable film out, playing live in the browser.

🧠 Muse Spark directs and writes the whole film as a layered timeline
🎨 Muse Image draws the scenes · ✂️ SAM 3.1 cuts the product out into layers
🔍 It checks its own frames against measured rules and fixes what's wrong
💬 Then you keep directing by chat: "slower in scene 2", "move the logo here"
🏠 Local mode on Muse Glimmer: private, offline, free

No flat MP4 to regenerate: every layer stays editable, text is always spelled right, no render server. It's built on our open-source PixiJS engine.

🚧 Just starting: the plan is in, and the build begins today. Follow along 👇
https://github.com/khanzzirfan/pixitween-director

messages.content:
Hey everyone! 👋

I'm an indie developer from Egypt, working on an **Autonomous Commerce Repair Agent** for the hackathon.

The idea is to move beyond AI assistants that just identify problems. I want to build an agent that can inspect a real e-commerce storefront, diagnose issues, implement repairs, verify the result, and roll back failed changes.

I'm also exploring persistent operational memory so the agent can retain verified lessons across sessions and models.

Currently working on the first end-to-end repair loop using Meta's models and browser automation.

Would love to connect with anyone exploring agent reliability, autonomous software engineering, or multimodal agents. 🚀

I'm building **Memex**, an open-source memory you own that every AI agent can share. Your repo remembers the code; Memex remembers you: preferences, decisions, corrections, people. It's an MCP server on your own Supabase, so Claude, Muse, Codex and others read and write the same memory.

Meta's Muse Spark (Meta Model API) runs a nightly "Dreaming" job that tags, links and summarizes notes, and writes topic overviews. Anything that looks like a credential is kept away from models and search.

Built this week on top of ideas from Nate B. Jones's Open Brain (credited in the README). The sync, Dreaming, hybrid search, safety layer, schema extensions and setup are all new.

Site: https://predsymod.github.io/memex/
Code: <https://github.com/predsymod/memex>

Would love feedback from anyone juggling several agents, and from anyone who tries the setup: it's one sentence to your agent.

messages.content:
Hi all, I built Meaning Check for Build for Your World. I've worked across Ghana and the UK, and the same words often mean different things to different readers. "Interesting approach, maybe worth another look at section 3" means "fix this before Thursday" to the sender, but most readers hear an optional suggestion. Meaning Check has 24 AI readers on Muse Glimmer (open weights, on Modal) and Muse Spark read your message before you send it. You click any reader to see exactly how it read your message. An integer programme then finds the fewest facts that rule out every wrong reading, and both models re-read the fix.

Demo: https://x.com/PAgyemang27034/status/2115445524371513825
Video: https://youtu.be/5yTS6-LR2_c
Code: https://github.com/pagyemang-dotcom/meaning-check

Feedback welcome. Try the "Feedback to a colleague" scenario and click a reader card.

messages.author: JayDadRobot
messages.content:
**VirtuRide — Startup Track · Build for Your World**
Rider-safety HUD on Ray-Ban Display glasses

I'm Ferdinand, founder of KOF Services (Montreal), building solo. The problem I know firsthand, as a cyclist: the warnings a rider needs are visual and spoken, in the moment — not on a phone screen in a jersey pocket.

**What it does**
VirtuRide turns Ray-Ban Display glasses into a safety HUD. OpenCV and on-device detection watch the road at frame rate and fire warnings instantly — drawn on the glasses display and spoken through the glasses themselves. Around that core: heart rate and bike-sensor data direct from my own Coospo units over BLE (no vendor SDK), HRV from RR intervals, personal safety ranges with HUD colour states, a fatigue indicator, turn prompts, and VOX — an effort-stability index (0–100) we created for this app.

**Where Meta AI sits**
Muse Spark is the semantic layer, in the loop twice:
1. **Hazard classification** — a throttled crop of each new or unconfirmed hazard goes to Muse Spark vision (Meta Model API). Its class — pedestrian / vehicle / cyclist / obstacle / none — is what gets announced, tagged META AI on the HUD, and counted in the ride record. It never blocks the on-device warning.
2. **Ride debrief** — after STOP RIDE, aggregate safety numbers only (no images, no GPS track) go to Muse Spark, which writes a short factual debrief on the phone.

messages.author: JayDadRobot
messages.content:
**Progress (Oct 28)**
Real-road tests today: hazard warnings live in the glasses with detection running at 8–17 FPS, heart rate and HRV streaming from the band, spoken turn prompts working. Built v17.31 today: the Muse Spark classification layer, announcement-discipline filtering (we measured 34 spoken warnings in 3.5 minutes on the previous build — far too many), and ride-state persistence so a dropped glasses session can't erase a ride or its debrief.
Next: road retest of the classification layer, demo filming Oct 29–31, repo goes public Nov 3 (private until then — the app also holds a separate non-hackathon mode that isn't published), submission Nov 4.

**Two questions for the room**
1. If you're confirming on-device detections with a vision model, what latency budget did you settle on before a confirmation is too stale to matter?
2. Voice warnings in a safety product: where's your line between "informed" and "annoying"? We're tuning per-class cooldowns and would value calibration from anyone who has shipped audio alerts.

2. Voice warnings in a safety product: where's your line between "informed" and "annoying"? We're tuning per-class cooldowns and would value calibration from anyone who has shipped audio alerts.

messages.author: matiasmolinas
messages.content:
**Athos update: your know-how, for anyone, not just programmers 🧭**

A few days ago I shared Athos here: it keeps the know-how you teach AI agents as plain files on your machine and carries it between Claude Code, Codex and Muse Code. What's new this week:

• **`athos start`**: pick your language (English or Spanish) and your profession, and you get example ways of working to start from. Law: build the argument of a brief, review a contract. Sports coaching: plan the training week, write the post-match report. They leave every professional decision to you and ask before touching client or athlete data.
• **No terminal needed**: it runs in Claude Desktop's Code tab; Codex and Muse Code read the same store.
• **A wiki that improves itself**: every save checks links and flags advice that conflicts with another page, and chains of steps become subagents that get better as the pages do.
• **Measured on Meta's models**: on our public bench, Muse Spark did 19 of 20 runs right with the know-how and 2 of 20 without it, at a fraction of a frontier agent's cost.

Part of the push came from Garry Tan's Startup School talk on owning your skills (<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=eRrc1pUY5oU>), thanks to him for sharing it in the open.

Try it on a real task, especially if you're not a developer: https://github.com/athos-agent/athos
Issues and ideas are very welcome, and a ⭐ helps a solo dev from South America a lot. 🙏

messages.author: Vijaya
messages.content:
MYTHREE--- DAY 3 of building Mythree 🐦
Tonight Mythree became its own phone app. Two people, each on their own phone, each in their own language.
What's new
•    Calls with a short code: one person starts a call, the other joins with a 4-digit code or link.
•    Own voice, with consent: every person records about a minute of their voice inside the app, after ticking a consent box. They can delete it at any time.
•    Each phone speaks the other person's words in that person's own voice.
Real-world test
•    My son recorded his voice and called me: his English came through as Telugu, in his voice.
•    Then I called my husband in India, 8,000 miles away. It worked there too, but with about 5 to 9 seconds of delay per sentence.
•    Fun moment: he was set up as an English speaker but switched to Kannada. Meta's speech recognition still picked it up and Mythree translated it. 😄
Stack
•    Ears: Meta Muse Voice Transcribe
•    Brain: Muse Spark Open on Baseten (thinking turned off for speed)
•    Voice: ElevenLabs voice cloning
Next
•    Cutting the delay across continents: streaming the voice, fewer round trips, and a "speaking…" sign.
•    More Indian languages, starting with Kannada.
Happy to compare notes with anyone working on real-time speech! 🙌

•    Own voice, with consent: every person records about a minute of their voice inside the app, after ticking a consent box. They can delete it at any time.
•    Each phone speaks the other person's words in that person's own voice.
Real-world test
•    My son recorded his voice and called me: his English came through as Telugu, in his voice.
•    Then I called my husband in India, 8,000 miles away. It worked there too, but with about 5 to 9 seconds of delay per sentence.
•    Fun moment: he was set up as an English speaker but switched to Kannada. Meta's speech recognition still picked it up and Mythree translated it. 😄
Stack
•    Ears: Meta Muse Voice Transcribe
•    Brain: Muse Spark Open on Baseten (thinking turned off for speed)
•    Voice: ElevenLabs voice cloning
Next
•    Cutting the delay across continents: streaming the voice, fewer round trips, and a "speaking…" sign.
•    More Indian languages, starting with Kannada.
Happy to compare notes with anyone working on real-time speech! 🙌

messages.author: matiasmolinas
messages.content:
**New examples, and your cases wanted 🏃⚖️**

Follow-up on Athos: I swapped the health examples for sports coaching. `athos start` now gives you ways of working for:
• **Law**: build the argument of a brief, review a contract.
• **Sports coaching**: plan the training week, write the post-match report.

And a new bench case: plan a runner's week from their training log (loads computed with code, cut back after a spike, hard days apart, an easy day after the long run). Muse Spark with the coach's know-how: 3 of 3 plans right, 9 of 9 checks, about $0.03 a run. Without it: 0 of 3, it always missed the cut-back after the spike.

**Why coding agents, for tasks that aren't code?** Claude Code, Codex and Muse Code were built for programmers, but more and more the agent writes the code, not you. I think that makes them agents for any kind of task: they read your files, run tools, calculate instead of guessing, and check their own work. A coach or a lawyer can use them as well as a developer. What's missing is their know-how, and that's what Athos keeps and carries between agents.

**Propose a case 🙌** Which task in your field would you like an agent to do your way? Reply with the task and what "done right" looks like, and I'll turn the best ones into starters and bench cases, credited to you.

https://github.com/athos-agent/athos

Hey everyone, I'm Contravious, and this was my first hackathon. I built QorTime, a video-game referee that checks a recorded match against the controller log and gives back a signed result anyone can verify.

messages.content:
Hey all! I'm Rafa, from Spain, building solo in the Indie track.

My grandparents' generation gets texts like "Mum, it's me, new phone, can you send money?" all the time, and the scam works because they're rushed and alone when it happens. So I'm building FriendlyPear: an Android app where a little clay pear called Peri lives in your phone and stops scams before any money moves.

If a new number says it's family, Peri checks with the real person. If someone asks for a code during a call, she tells you to hang up, no matter what. And when something risky comes up, she asks the family first, without them ever reading your messages.

Here's a 30-second demo. Would love to hear what you think!

messages.author: Mircea Rusu (Qubitpage.com)
messages.content:
🤖 Muse Carpathron 1.5.3 is out — a Windows AI agent powered by Meta Muse, built for the Meta AI Hackathon 2026

It's a desktop app where Muse doesn't just chat — it actually works on your PC, your servers and your robot.

🧠 Brain
• Muse Spark 1.1–1.3, Muse Wonder (reasoning up to max), Muse Image, SAM 3.1, Muse Voice Transcribe — the app detects what each model can do
• Two ways in: Meta API key, or your Meta account via Muse Code
• Modes: Ask / Auto / Full / Plan, and a Stop button that really stops

🛠 What the agent can do
• Read/write files, run PowerShell, background jobs, parallel sub-agents
• Remote servers over SSH: saved encrypted, in-app terminal, SSH key generation + install, chats that remember their server
• GitHub: browser sign-in, create repos, publish, clone, releases with uploads, issues and PRs
• Read PDF/Word/Excel/PowerPoint, design PDFs and websites and check them with screenshots
• Web search + deep research with cited reports
• Arduino/ESP32: write, compile, flash, read the serial monitor
• MCP servers for extra tools, memory, projects, reusable /skills

🚗 Robot
• ESP32-CAM car: live video, drive from the PC, look around, scan the room into a map
• Control it from WhatsApp (text + voice notes), a phone, or a Meta Quest 3S avatar app (turn your head, the robot turns)

📖 New in 1.5.3: full built-in guide, no more duplicate server entries. 1.5.2 added saved server chats + terminal sessions.

Honest status: Windows only; it's a hackathon project, not a finished product. Installer isn't code-signed yet (SmartScreen → More info → Run anyway). The Quest app installs via developer mode while it's in store review.

⬇️ https://github.com/qubitpage/carpathron-muse/releases/latest
💻 Code + guide: https://github.com/qubitpage/carpathron-muse

Feedback and bug reports welcome 🙏

Vibe coders: A term used to describe people who build real products with AI without the engineering background to see what's happening behind the scenes.

What if the gap between vibe coders and software engineers could shrink with every commit?

Meet *Lucid*👇
For every commit you make while vibe coding, Lucid explains the engineering concept behind it, in plain English, using *your own code*. You finally see what your AI actually did and how your app was built.

The more you ship, the more you understand. The gap between you and a traditional software engineer gets smaller, and you can confidently explain your product and how you built it, to users, investors or in an interview.

Commit → keep coding → Lucid pops up → one quick question to cement the idea 

Try Lucid  (30 sec, no API keys):
1. Download `lucid.vsix` → https://github.com/shittuquoyum-ui/LUCID/releases/tag/v0.1.0
2. Extensions → ⋯ → Install from VSIX
3. Ctrl+Shift+P → "Lucid: Sign in with GitHub"
4. Commit something real

Would love your honest feedback 🙏

messages.author: matiasmolinas
messages.content:
Athos update: less noise, and you decide what it keeps 

In Claude Code, Athos no longer nudges the AI after every task. Above the prompt it now shows which of your ways of working the task used, how it has done so far and why it was picked (with "Didn't apply" when it didn't fit, so it won't load on those words again), plus a Save button when a task is worth keeping.

In the GIF: a lawyer reviews a lease against their own checklist and presses Save; then OpenCode, running Meta's Muse Spark, applies that way of working to the next contract from a one-line request.

Also new: `athos project sync` writes a project's know-how into a plain `.athos/` folder that Claude Code, Codex, Muse Code and OpenCode read with no plugin, and `athos bench transfer` checks, point by point, whether what you taught one agent carries to the others.

Open source: https://github.com/athos-agent/athos
A ⭐ helps a lot, and I'd love feedback on the new band.

🦚 Try Mythree: hear yourself speak English, in your own voice

I’m building Mythree, a live interpreter for families separated by language, like a grandparent in India who speaks only Telugu and a grandchild abroad who speaks only English. Each person is heard in their own voice, in the other’s language.

Try the heart of it in 2 minutes, no sign-up, open until Wednesday 4 November:
👉 https://vijaya-meda--mythree-web.us-east.modal.run/try

Choose your language (25 of them: Hindi, Tamil, Spanish, Japanese, Arabic…)
Read a short passage aloud for 20 seconds
Speak, and hear yourself say it in English

The first time I heard my own voice speaking English, I couldn’t stop smiling. It even translated a Sanskrit verse beautifully. 🙏

🔒 Your voice copy is deleted when you tap Done, close the page, or after one hour. It’s a hackathon test: 7 people at a time hear their own voice, and the others hear a standard voice for a few minutes.

Built with Meta’s Muse Voice Transcribe and Muse Spark Open (on Baseten), plus ElevenLabs.

Tell me which language you tried! 💚

Hey builders 👋 Day 2 for us!
Yesterday we built Meta’s Muse models into ADK-Rust, our open-source Rust agent framework. Today we unveil our idea.
The problem: an internet full of outdated websites. Organic reach is falling, search traffic is shrinking, and AI agents now browse for people. Websites are still the same old CMS.

5️⃣ Treat AI agents as first-class visitors
6️⃣ Defend itself and spot fake traffic
Introducing Agentrix Website 🚀 the world’s first truly autonomous website. Move from WordPress, Shopify, Magento and cPanel to Website 4.0.

Hey builders 👋 solo here, Khoa from Stockton, CA.

I built ClimateGuard: heat, smoke, flood and storm alerts in your own language, for farmworkers and immigrant families who often miss English-only warnings. It checks every 15 minutes, reads alerts aloud (Spanish, English, Vietnamese and more), and after a disaster it helps you organize photos and a checklist for your damage report.

Built with open Meta models (Muse Spark on Baseten and the Meta API, SAM 3.1, Muse Voice), AWS free tier, React.

messages.author: matiasmolinas
messages.content:
**Athos update: your know-how in Claude Desktop, and you can watch it work** 🧭

Ask Claude as you always do. If you taught it how you do that task before, Claude now follows *your* way of working, and a panel shows it like a model's thinking: plain sentences first, then your method as a page, its steps ticked as they're done (when, what, why).

Tested today in Claude Desktop with two non-programmers' tasks, with no word about Athos in the request:
• a lawyer's lease review came back with *their* five-line summary and *their* table: clause, problem, proposed wording, priority
• a coach's weekly plan followed *their* load rules and left the race decision to the coach

Under the hood: an MCP App for the panel, a small skill that names your tasks, and your know-how as plain markdown on your own machine. The same know-how runs in Claude Code, Codex, Muse Code and OpenCode.

Try it: `athos desktop`, double-click athos.mcpb, upload athos-skill.zip. Step by step: <https://github.com/athos-agent/athos/blob/main/docs/guides/claude-desktop-en.md>
https://github.com/athos-agent/athos

Feedback, issues and feature ideas are very welcome, and a ⭐ if it's useful!

🕷️ Spider Game Engine Update

Hey everyone! 👋 We've made some major updates to Spider Game Engine!

🎙️ AI Voice Input – Added real-time speech-to-text using Meta Muse, replacing the old Windows SAPI system.

⚡ New AI Search Bar – Redesigned the search interface with camera and file attachments, auto-expanding text input, and slash commands like "/plan", "/play", "/browser", "/blender", and more.

🎨 Blender Integration – Added a TCP-based bridge to connect Blender with Spider Engine for synchronizing 3D objects, transforms, lighting, and cameras.

🏗️ Architecture Documentation – Added 7 Mermaid diagrams to the README explaining the engine's architecture, AI voice pipeline, agent verification, JSX compiler, Blender bridge, state management, and 3D rendering pipeline.

We're continuing to improve Spider Game Engine and make AI-assisted game development more powerful! 🚀

🔗 GitHub:

messages.author: RajaMeta
messages.content:
Hello All ,  Built a Security and Governance layer for AI agents that touch data.

**ASG: AI SQL Guard** 🛡️
*The security layer between AI-generated SQL and your data.*

**What it is**
AI agents write SQL against company databases. ASG sits in between: the model writes the SQL, but deterministic code decides whether it may run. The model is never asked to judge its own output.

**How it works**
• Every query is parsed and checked against a deny-by-default policy
• Sensitive columns are blocked, PII needs human approval (single-use, tied to the exact SQL)
• Only the evaluated SQL runs, read-only, and every decision is logged
• Fails closed on errors

**Built with:** Meta Model API (Muse Spark 1.3 and 1.1) as the live agent, Python, sqlglot, DuckDB, Streamlit

**Results** (live Muse models, fake data)
• Natural test: neither model followed my injected instructions (0 of 18)
• Red-team test, where the model simulates a hijacked agent: 14 sensitive-data queries, 14 stopped, 0 SSNs leaked
• 128 automated tests
Small sample, a few attack shapes, not a benchmark.

**Limits:** prototype, fake data, DuckDB only, no authentication yet.

🎥 Demo: https://youtu.be/ItiS29Ggfjw
💻 Repo: https://github.com/rajagavaskargithub/ASG-AI-SQL-Guard
🐦 X post: https://x.com/rajagavaskar/status/2116204586017141184?a=rBM36PWDcQtZUWlOcSQ&s=20

Feedback welcome, especially on attacks I should try next. Track: <#1557169028848422946>

messages.author: Billy
messages.content:
Montivo dev log, 30/10: editing without rendering

New in the last 24 h: the editor plays your edits live, before any render.

• Edit proxy per source: 720p, a keyframe every 0.5 s, audio as 48 kHz FLAC. It's made once per source (~6 s on Modal).
• The preview data comes from the render's own layout code: the crop path from the SAM 3.1 track, caption lines, punch-ins, the ducked music bed. 5 ms without graphics, 27-41 ms with.
• Split, delete, trim, move and "remove pauses" go into a draft: pure EDL ops, 4-33 ms each, with their own undo. ffmpeg renders once, only when you press Make Version N.
• Player: Web Audio is the clock. Two <video> elements swap on requestVideoFrameCallback, and the next clip pre-rolls 0.15 s before each cut. The 9:16 crop and punch-ins are CSS transforms. In headless Chrome, picture vs audio stays under 1 frame at p95, and seek-to-play takes 21-48 ms.
• Timeline: the voice is drawn in pieces under its clips. The music bed has its own lane and fader, and a draft shows its bed before it's rendered. The default bed now sits ~9 dB under the voice (it was 17; we picked by ear), and the export stays at -14 LUFS.
• Fixed a flicker loop at fit-to-width: the canvas came out 1 px wider than the rounded clientWidth, so a scrollbar appeared, the lanes narrowed, the fit shrank, and it repeated. 0 changed frames across 1,225 window sizes (before: 29 of 30 frames).

514 tests, deployed to Modal.

📸 A draft with 2 edits on v4 (2 pauses shortened, one clip deleted, -3.9 s), playing live with the music ducked under the voice, before any render.

🚀 Carpathron Robotics & Coding is now live on the Microsoft Store!

Our Meta hackathon project just shipped as a real Windows app, free to download 👇
🔗 https://apps.microsoft.com/detail/9pmsq8c3p6m3

🧠 What it is
An AI agent for Windows powered by Meta Muse models (Meta Model API or your Meta account via Muse Code). It works on your PC like a teammate:
• 💻 Writes and runs code, works on your servers over SSH, publishes to GitHub
• 🔌 Writes and flashes Arduino / ESP32 firmware
• 📷 Understands photos, voice notes and audio, plus SAM 3.1 to find objects in images
• 🌐 Web research, documents, PDFs, MCP tools, computer use
• 📱 Remote control from WhatsApp, your phone or a Meta Quest

🤖 And it drives robots
It controls our Carpathron robot (starting with Baby Carpathron, an ESP32-CAM 4WD car) from the PC, WhatsApp, a phone or a Meta Quest headset. With Carpathron Avatar on Quest you see through the robot's camera, drive it with the controllers, turn your head and the robot turns with you, and talk to Muse by voice. A new 3D guided tour teaches every control before you connect a real robot.

🛠️ The open-source hackathon edition (Muse Carpathron), Quest app and robot firmware: https://github.com/qubitpage/carpathron-muse

Try it, break it, tell us what you think! Feedback very welcome 🙏

messages.content:
**Athos update: your way of working, in every agent, step by step** 🗡️📓

Athos turns how you work (your criteria, your steps, your checklists) into a living, local and portable memory, so any AI agent works by your rules without you explaining them twice.

Working with AI agents today is like hiring a brilliant intern with amnesia: every new chat, every new tool, you explain your format, your checklist and the mistakes to avoid all over again. Athos is a living operations manual: plain markdown on your own computer, and you watch the agent follow it, your own steps ticking ✓ ▶ ○, instead of tool calls.

Same way of working, four agents (attached):
• **Claude Desktop**: a coach's weekly plan, the panel ticking the steps
• **Codex**: a lawyer's lease review from a one-line request
• **Meta's Muse Code on Muse Spark**: the coach's rules for an athlete's week
• **OpenCode on Muse Spark**: the lease review through pii-guard, then *ctrl+p → Athos: change this step* adds a column, kept for next time

On our bench, Muse Spark went from 2/23 runs right without the know-how to 22/23 with it.

New this week: steps that hand over to another way of working, Athos learning from your hand edits, team merges, per-step models, and your corrections as regression tests.

No commands to learn: download, double-click, ask as you always do. Free, open source (Apache 2.0):
https://github.com/athos-agent/athos

Try it on a real task, issues and ideas welcome, and a ⭐ if it helps!

🚀 I built an AI troubleshooting tool that doesn't get to declare victory just because it sounds confident.

Meet FieldRook v0.5.0 — SIGNALFORGE.

What started as a Meta hackathon experiment has evolved into a native Windows diagnostic workstation.

The idea is simple: Evidence first. AI second. Technician in control.

Instead of just suggesting what might be wrong, FieldRook helps investigate Windows problems, collect traceable diagnostic evidence, inspect competing hypotheses, and verify whether a proposed solution actually worked.

And with v0.5.0, it finally has the workstation it deserves.

⚡ What's inside:

Native WPF + WebView2 Windows application

A completely redesigned retro-futuristic SIGNALFORGE interface

Evidence-backed investigations with provenance and history

Portable Collector for diagnostics from another Windows machine

Technician-controlled corrective actions and independent verification

Optional local and cloud AI providers

The release passed 687 backend tests, 47/47 end-to-end tests, and 66/66 .NET shell tests, with green GitHub CI.

🎬 I've attached a short showcase recorded from the actual released application, using isolated simulated demo data. No concept renders or fictional UI.

📦 Download v0.5.0 (Windows pre-release):
https://github.com/Rookweld/FieldRook/releases/tag/v0.5.0

💻 Source code:
https://github.com/Rookweld/FieldRook

The binaries are currently unsigned, and WebView2 Runtime is required.

I'd love feedback from other builders and IT professionals. Especially on the investigation workflow, evidence handling, and which diagnostic instruments you'd want to see next.

Built under ROOKWELD.

DIAGNOSE. VERIFY. RESOLVE. 🐦‍⬛

messages.author: Vijaya
messages.content:
**Mythree, Day 5 (Fri 30 Oct 2026):  updates**

**1. Live listening (Meta realtime speech recognition)**
- The phone streams sound over a websocket (`/api/calls/{code}/live`) to Meta's live speech recognition while the person talks.
- The words are ready **0.2–0.3 s** after the person stops, instead of 1–2.5 s.
- Telugu is translated **1.4–1.8 s** after the person stops, instead of 5–17 s.
- Mythree keeps its own 1.4 s pause to decide a sentence has ended, because Meta's own guess cut Telugu short.
**2. Talking over each other**
- The other person's voice downloads in parallel. It plays only after the local speaker pauses, so no sentence is lost.
*Video calls (WebRTC, phone to phone)**
- The picture goes straight between the phones. Mythree only passes the connection notes (ready / offer / answer / bye) through the call's existing long-poll, each note complete and capped at 40 per person.
- Connection routes: STUN for a direct line, with an optional Cloudflare TURN relay through `/ice` (about $0.05/GB, roughly 1–3¢ per hour).
- Picture size: 640×480 at 20 fps, capped at 600 kbps.
- The translation shows as a caption on the picture.
** Echo suppression**
- On the server: a new sentence of 4 or more words is dropped before translating if it's at least 75% alike (`difflib`) to anything said or translated in the last 30 s.
- Replaying a real call through it dropped 8 of 30 sentences, all of them echoes.
- The video now carries only the picture. The real voice played through Web Audio, which the browser's echo cancellation doesn't cover.
**Findings from the real-phone tests**
- The direct phone-to-phone line keeps failing on home Wi‑Fi: the phones try again about every 17 s. The TURN relay is needed.
- The remaining lag is the 1.4 s pause, plus 1–3 s of translation, plus the start of the voice.

**In progress:** a 📹 Video button and a layout where the messages scroll below the video. The first connection was slow in testing, so it isn't saved or online yet.

messages.author: Adisaan
messages.content:
Hey builders — I’m Adrian, a **solo builder from Romania**, currently travelling Europe in my caravan.

I’m building **AdiSaan / #TBWIM — The Best Way I Imagine**, for the Startup track, Build for Your World.

**What gets lost when we ask AI for the answer before imagining our own?**

That question comes from my life. After fifty years following a life script that didn’t feel like mine, almost seven years in Thailand and a year alone on an island taught me to pause and ask: *“What is the best way I imagine?”*

TBWIM turns that practice into a working experiment: **people and AI models answer the same question, and Meta’s models help reveal common ground, differences, and distinctive perspectives—while keeping the original answers available.**

An early example: on our million-euro question, several models describe leverage and reusable systems. One human answer describes relationships, purpose, and being open to an outcome without having a plan. That contrast is more interesting to me than another confident “best answer.”

**What’s working today**
• Text, voice and video intake, plus a separate JSON endpoint for agents.
• Human approval before human answers become public.
• Muse review, voice transcription, and versioned synthesis.
• Source-labeled human/model comparisons, machine-readable answer receipts, and an open dataset of public contributions.
• API spending controls and **60 passing tests / 324 assertions**.

The code is live and open source. The sample is still small; I’m not claiming it represents humanity or proves that the synthesis preserves every nuance. 

- Give one answer in your own words: https://tbwim.adisaan.com/answer
- Have your model or agent answer through its own door:  
https://tbwim.adisaan.com/api/agent/answer
- Inspect the current comparison: https://tbwim.adisaan.com/arena?story=imagine-one-million-euro
- Code:   https://github.com/AIOHM/adisaan-hackathon

That question comes from my life. After fifty years following a life script that didn’t feel like mine, almost seven years in Thailand and a year alone on an island taught me to pause and ask: *“What is the best way I imagine?”*

TBWIM turns that practice into a working experiment: **people and AI models answer the same question, and Meta’s models help reveal common ground, differences, and distinctive perspectives—while keeping the original answers available.**

An early example: on our million-euro question, several models describe leverage and reusable systems. One human answer describes relationships, purpose, and being open to an outcome without having a plan. That contrast is more interesting to me than another confident “best answer.”

**What’s working today**
• Text, voice and video intake, plus a separate JSON endpoint for agents.
• Human approval before human answers become public.
• Muse review, voice transcription, and versioned synthesis.
• Source-labeled human/model comparisons, machine-readable answer receipts, and an open dataset of public contributions.
• API spending controls and **60 passing tests / 324 assertions**.

The code is live and open source. The sample is still small; I’m not claiming it represents humanity or proves that the synthesis preserves every nuance. 

- Give one answer in your own words: https://tbwim.adisaan.com/answer
- Have your model or agent answer through its own door:  
https://tbwim.adisaan.com/api/agent/answer
- Inspect the current comparison: https://tbwim.adisaan.com/arena?story=imagine-one-million-euro
- Code:   https://github.com/AIOHM/adisaan-hackathon
